subject.title: [Feature]: Audit log for agent memory changes

question: What memory mutation audit contract should OpenClaw support for MEMORY.md and memory/*.md writes, including storage boundary, integrity model, redaction policy, and cause propagation?
rationale: The security value depends on tamper boundaries, privacy tradeoffs, and whether the audit belongs in memory-core, a plugin SDK seam, or a broader persistence-provenance layer; source inspection cannot choose that product/security contract safely.

options.title: Design first-class memory audit
options.body: Keep this issue open and specify storage, integrity, redaction, and event schema before accepting an implementation.

options.title: Fold into persistence provenance
options.body: Track this under the broader persistent-state provenance and before_persistence_write design if maintainers want one architecture for memory, files, preferences, and tasks.

options.title: Externalize to plugin or MCP
options.body: Close or narrow core work only if maintainers decide existing plugin/MCP surfaces are sufficient for memory-audit packages without new OpenClaw contracts.

recommendation.title: Design first-class memory audit
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and specify storage, integrity, redaction, and event schema before accepting an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already routed this as first-class memory/security design and is connected to the adjacent memory-flush surface.
